claim: The establishment of separated pulmonary and systemic circulation in vertebrates via cardiac outflow tract (OFT) septation accounts for 10% of all congenital anomalies.
source: The establishment of separated pulmonary and systemic circulation in vertebrates, via cardiac outflow tract (OFT) septation, is a sensitive developmental process accounting for 10% of all congenital anomalies.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that provides a statistical claim about the prevalence of OFT septation defects among congenital anomalies.

claim: Neural Crest Cells (NCC) colonising the heart condensate along the primitive endocardial tube and force its scission into two tubes.
source: Neural Crest Cells (NCC) colonising the heart condensate along the primitive endocardial tube and force its scission into two tubes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the mechanism by which NCCs contribute to OFT septation.

claim: NCC aggregation progressively decreases along the OFT distal-proximal axis following a BMP signalling gradient.
source: Here, we show that NCC aggregation progressively decreases along the OFT distal-proximal axis following a BMP signalling gradient.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing P-Smad1/5/8 levels and NCC condensation patterns along the OFT axis.

claim: Dullard tunes the BMP gradient amplitude and prevents NCC premature condensation.
source: Dullard, a nuclear phosphatase, tunes the BMP gradient amplitude and prevents NCC premature condensation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing increased P-Smad1/5/8 levels and premature NCC condensation in Dullard mutants.

claim: Dullard maintains transcriptional programs providing NCC with mesenchymal traits.
source: Dullard maintains transcriptional programs providing NCC with mesenchymal traits.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell qPCR data showing downregulation of mesenchymal markers in Dullard mutant NCCs.

claim: Dullard attenuates the expression of the aggregation factor Sema3c.
source: It attenuates the expression of the aggregation factor Sema3c and conversely promotes that of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition driver Twist1.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and qPCR data showing elevated Sema3c expression in Dullard mutants.

claim: Dullard promotes the expression of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition driver Twist1.
source: It attenuates the expression of the aggregation factor Sema3c and conversely promotes that of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition driver Twist1.
evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling and single-cell qPCR data showing reduced Twist1 expression in Dullard mutants.

claim: Dullard-mediated fine-tuning of BMP signalling ensures the timed and progressive zipper-like closure of the OFT by the NCC.
source: Altogether, Dullard-mediated fine-tuning of BMP signalling ensures the timed and progressive zipper-like closure of the OFT by the NCC and prevents the formation of a heart carrying the congenital abnormalities defining the tetralogy of Fallot.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the integration of multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of Dullard in cardiac NCC prevents the formation of a heart carrying the congenital abnormalities defining the tetralogy of Fallot.
source: Altogether, Dullard-mediated fine-tuning of BMP signalling ensures the timed and progressive zipper-like closure of the OFT by the NCC and prevents the formation of a heart carrying the congenital abnormalities defining the tetralogy of Fallot.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis of Dullard mutant hearts showing features of tetralogy of Fallot.

claim: Faulty septation of the OFT represents 30% of all congenital heart diseases.
source: As such, faulty septation of the OFT represents 30% of all congenital heart diseases, with poor clinical prognosis due to improper mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
evidence: This is a statistical claim about the prevalence of OFT septation defects among congenital heart diseases.

claim: Faulty septation of the OFT has poor clinical prognosis due to improper mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
source: As such, faulty septation of the OFT represents 30% of all congenital heart diseases, with poor clinical prognosis due to improper mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical consequences of OFT septation defects based on established medical knowledge.

claim: The OFT initially forms a solitary tube called truncus arteriosus.
source: Initially, forming a solitary tube called truncus arteriosus, it gets progressively remodelled into two tubes which give rise to the aortic (Ao) and pulmonary (Pa) arteries (Brickner et al., 2000; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of normal OFT development supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: The truncus arteriosus gets progressively remodelled into two tubes which give rise to the aortic and pulmonary arteries.
source: Initially, forming a solitary tube called truncus arteriosus, it gets progressively remodelled into two tubes which give rise to the aortic (Ao) and pulmonary (Pa) arteries (Brickner et al., 2000; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Morphogenesis of the OFT is orchestrated by cross-interaction between several cell types including the myocardial progenitors of the second heart field (SHF), the endocardial cells (EC), and the cardiac neural crest cells (cardiac NCC).
source: Morphogenesis of the OFT is orchestrated in time and space by cross-interaction between several cell types including the myocardial progenitors of the second heart field (SHF), the endocardial cells (EC) delineating the OFT lumen, and the cardiac neural crest cells (cardiac NCC) (Kelly, 2012; Keyte and Hutson, 2012; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a summary statement about OFT morphogenesis supported by citations.

claim: Various genetic manipulations or ablation models have highlighted the predominant role of cardiac NCC in initiating and controlling OFT septation.
source: Various genetic manipulations or ablation models have highlighted the predominant role of cardiac NCC in initiating and controlling OFT septation (Bockman et al., 1987; Phillips et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a summary of previous research findings supported by citations.

claim: Cardiac NCC delaminate from the dorsal neural tube and migrate through the pharyngeal mesoderm to reach the developing OFT.
source: Originally, cardiac NCC delaminate from the dorsal neural tube and migrate through the pharyngeal mesoderm to reach the developing OFT (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the migration pattern of cardiac NCCs, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Cardiac NCC invade the two cardiac cushions, condense toward the endocardium and trigger its rupture, thereby inducing cardiac cushions fusion and creating the two great arteries.
source: There, they invade the two cardiac cushions, condense toward the endocardium and trigger its rupture, thereby inducing cardiac cushions fusion and creating the two great arteries (Plein et al., 2015; Waldo et al., 1998).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of OFT septation by cardiac NCCs, supported by citations.

claim: The rupture of the endocardium is first detected in the regions of the OFT which are the most distal from the heart chambers.
source: The rupture of the endocardium is first detected in the regions of the OFT which are the most distal from the heart chambers.
evidence: This describes the spatial pattern of endocardial rupture during OFT septation.

claim: In mouse embryos, endocardial rupture initiates around 11.5 days of embryonic development (E11.5).
source: In mouse embryos this rupture initiates around 11.5 days of embryonic development (E11.5; Figure 1A) and then expands progressively to more proximal levels.
evidence: This provides a specific developmental timepoint for endocardial rupture in mice.

claim: Endocardial rupture expands progressively to more proximal levels of the OFT.
source: In mouse embryos this rupture initiates around 11.5 days of embryonic development (E11.5; Figure 1A) and then expands progressively to more proximal levels.
evidence: This describes the temporal progression of endocardial rupture along the OFT axis.

claim: NCC differentiate into the vascular smooth muscles of the aortic arch.
source: In parallel to these morphogenetic events, NCC differentiate into the vascular smooth muscles of the aortic arch (Keyte and Hutson, 2012) and also contribute to the arterial valves (Odelin et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes one differentiation fate of cardiac NCCs, supported by citation.

claim: NCC contribute to the arterial valves.
source: In parallel to these morphogenetic events, NCC differentiate into the vascular smooth muscles of the aortic arch (Keyte and Hutson, 2012) and also contribute to the arterial valves (Odelin et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes another contribution of cardiac NCCs, supported by citation.

claim: Bone Morphogenic Proteins (BMP) are secreted by the outlying myocardium cells from E8.75 onwards.
source: Intense investigations to identify the molecular cues controlling the stereotyped behaviour and differentiation of cardiac NCC in the OFT have established the importance of the Bone Morphogenic Proteins (BMP), secreted by the outlying myocardium cells from E8.75 onwards (Danesh et al., 2009; Jiao et al., 2003; Liu et al., 2004; McCulley et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the source and timing of BMP secretion during OFT development, supported by citations.

claim: Ablation of the BMP receptor Bmpr1a in the NCC lineage leads to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT.
source: Indeed, ablation of the BMP receptor Bmpr1a, ablation of the key downstream transcriptional effector Smad4, or forced expression of the BMP signalling antagonist Smad7 within the NCC lineage all lead to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT, thus phenocopying cardiac NCC ablation experiments (Jia et al., 2007; Stottmann et al., 2004; Tang et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the phenotype resulting from loss of BMP signaling in NCCs, supported by citations.

claim: Ablation of Smad4 in the NCC lineage leads to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT.
source: Indeed, ablation of the BMP receptor Bmpr1a, ablation of the key downstream transcriptional effector Smad4, or forced expression of the BMP signalling antagonist Smad7 within the NCC lineage all lead to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT, thus phenocopying cardiac NCC ablation experiments (Jia et al., 2007; Stottmann et al., 2004; Tang et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the phenotype resulting from loss of BMP signaling in NCCs, supported by citations.

claim: Forced expression of the BMP signalling antagonist Smad7 in the NCC lineage leads to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT.
source: Indeed, ablation of the BMP receptor Bmpr1a, ablation of the key downstream transcriptional effector Smad4, or forced expression of the BMP signalling antagonist Smad7 within the NCC lineage all lead to the formation of hypoplastic cushions, a shorter and non-septated OFT, thus phenocopying cardiac NCC ablation experiments (Jia et al., 2007; Stottmann et al., 2004; Tang et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the phenotype resulting from inhibition of BMP signaling in NCCs, supported by citations.

claim: Knock-out of the ligand BMP4 from the myocardium prevents OFT septation.
source: Knock-out of the ligand BMP4 from the myocardium similarly prevents OFT septation (Liu et al., 2004).
evidence: This describes the phenotype resulting from loss of BMP4 in the myocardium, supported by citation.

claim: Dullard (Ctdnep1) is a perinuclear phosphatase that functions as a negative intracellular BMP inhibitor.
source: To gain insights into these molecular cascades, we decided to dissect the role of Dullard (Ctdnep1), a perinuclear phosphatase that functions as a negative intracellular BMP inhibitor, during OFT morphogenesis (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Urrutia et al., 2016; Sardi et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the function of Dullard, supported by citations.

claim: Binding of BMP ligands to their transmembrane receptors leads to the phosphorylation of the transcription factors Smad1/5/8.
source: In the canonical BMP signalling cascade, binding of BMP ligands to their transmembrane receptors leads to the phosphorylation of the transcription factors Smad1/5/8 which translocate to the nucleus and modify the transcriptional landscape of targeted cells (Bruce and Sapkota, 2012).
evidence: This describes the canonical BMP signaling pathway, supported by citation.

claim: Phosphorylated Smad1/5/8 translocate to the nucleus and modify the transcriptional landscape of targeted cells.
source: In the canonical BMP signalling cascade, binding of BMP ligands to their transmembrane receptors leads to the phosphorylation of the transcription factors Smad1/5/8 which translocate to the nucleus and modify the transcriptional landscape of targeted cells (Bruce and Sapkota, 2012).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of action of phosphorylated Smads, supported by citation.

claim: Dullard is one of the few cytoplasmic modulators of Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation.
source: Dullard stands out as one of the few cytoplasmic modulators of this phosphorylation step, which also includes PP1A, PP2B, the inhibitory Smads 6 and 7 and the Ubiquitin degradation pathway (Bruce and Sapkota, 2012).
evidence: This describes the role of Dullard in the context of other BMP signaling modulators, supported by citation.

claim: The Dullard protein is evolutionary conserved from yeast to mammals.
source: The Dullard protein is evolutionary conserved from yeast to mammals and expressed in many embryonic tissues, including the developing neural tube and neural crest cells (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Satow et al., 2006; Tanaka et al., 2013; Urrutia et al., 2016; Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the evolutionary conservation of Dullard, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard is expressed in many embryonic tissues, including the developing neural tube and neural crest cells.
source: The Dullard protein is evolutionary conserved from yeast to mammals and expressed in many embryonic tissues, including the developing neural tube and neural crest cells (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Satow et al., 2006; Tanaka et al., 2013; Urrutia et al., 2016; Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of Dullard, supported by citations and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Evidence from Drosophila, xenopus, and mouse embryos indicates that Dullard dampens Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation levels upon BMP stimulation.
source: Several pieces of evidence from Drosophila, xenopus, and mouse embryos indicate that this enzyme dampens Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation levels upon BMP stimulation (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Satow et al., 2006; Urrutia et al., 2016).
evidence: This summarizes evidence from multiple model organisms, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard's activity on BMP signaling is likely to be tissue specific.
source: However, this activity is likely to be tissue specific, as depleting Dullard in gastrulating mouse embryos or later in the limb bud mesenchyme did not impair BMP signalling, while its depletion in the mouse embryonic kidney led to an elevated BMP response (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the context-dependent effects of Dullard on BMP signaling, supported by citations.

claim: Depleting Dullard in gastrulating mouse embryos did not impair BMP signalling.
source: However, this activity is likely to be tissue specific, as depleting Dullard in gastrulating mouse embryos or later in the limb bud mesenchyme did not impair BMP signalling, while its depletion in the mouse embryonic kidney led to an elevated BMP response (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the effect of Dullard depletion in a specific context, supported by citations.

claim: Depleting Dullard in the limb bud mesenchyme did not impair BMP signalling.
source: However, this activity is likely to be tissue specific, as depleting Dullard in gastrulating mouse embryos or later in the limb bud mesenchyme did not impair BMP signalling, while its depletion in the mouse embryonic kidney led to an elevated BMP response (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the effect of Dullard depletion in a specific context, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard depletion in the mouse embryonic kidney led to an elevated BMP response.
source: However, this activity is likely to be tissue specific, as depleting Dullard in gastrulating mouse embryos or later in the limb bud mesenchyme did not impair BMP signalling, while its depletion in the mouse embryonic kidney led to an elevated BMP response (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the effect of Dullard depletion in a specific context, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard is required for the expansion of extraembryonic tissues.
source: Early in development, it is required for the expansion of extraembryonic tissues, and later on, it prevents cell death by apoptosis in kidney nephrons or favours the ossification of limb bones (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a developmental role of Dullard, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard prevents cell death by apoptosis in kidney nephrons.
source: Early in development, it is required for the expansion of extraembryonic tissues, and later on, it prevents cell death by apoptosis in kidney nephrons or favours the ossification of limb bones (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a developmental role of Dullard, supported by citations.

claim: Dullard favours the ossification of limb bones.
source: Early in development, it is required for the expansion of extraembryonic tissues, and later on, it prevents cell death by apoptosis in kidney nephrons or favours the ossification of limb bones (Sakaguchi et al., 2013; Tanaka et al., 2013; Hayata et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a developmental role of Dullard, supported by citations.

claim: Deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC increases Smad1/5/8 activity.
source: We showed here that deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC increases Smad1/5/8 activity, leading to premature and asymmetric septation of the OFT and pulmonary artery closure.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing increased P-Smad1/5/8 levels in Dullard mutant NCCs.

claim: Deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC leads to premature and asymmetric septation of the OFT.
source: We showed here that deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC increases Smad1/5/8 activity, leading to premature and asymmetric septation of the OFT and pulmonary artery closure.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing OFT morphological defects in Dullard mutants.

claim: Deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC leads to pulmonary artery closure.
source: We showed here that deletion of Dullard in the cardiac NCC increases Smad1/5/8 activity, leading to premature and asymmetric septation of the OFT and pulmonary artery closure.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing pulmonary artery obstruction in Dullard mutants.

claim: BMP overactivation in the cardiac NCC occurs concurrently with the downregulation of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Rac1, Mmp14 and Cdh2).
source: BMP overactivation in the cardiac NCC occurs concurrently with the downregulation of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Rac1, Mmp14 and Cdh2) and upregulation of Sema3c, which is associated with premature cardiac NCC condensation to the endocardium.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell qPCR and in situ hybridization data showing reduced expression of these markers in Dullard mutants.

claim: BMP overactivation in the cardiac NCC is associated with upregulation of Sema3c.
source: BMP overactivation in the cardiac NCC occurs concurrently with the downregulation of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Rac1, Mmp14 and Cdh2) and upregulation of Sema3c, which is associated with premature cardiac NCC condensation to the endocardium.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and qPCR data showing elevated Sema3c expression in Dullard mutants.

claim: Upregulation of Sema3c is associated with premature cardiac NCC condensation to the endocardium.
source: BMP overactivation in the cardiac NCC occurs concurrently with the downregulation of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Rac1, Mmp14 and Cdh2) and upregulation of Sema3c, which is associated with premature cardiac NCC condensation to the endocardium.
evidence: This is supported by the correlation between Sema3c expression and NCC condensation patterns observed in the data.

claim: Graded BMP activity, Sema3c expression and cardiac NCC condensation along the OFT axis set the tempo of OFT septation from its distal to its proximal regions.
source: Our data converge to a model whereby graded BMP activity, Sema3c expression and cardiac NCC condensation along the OFT axis set the tempo of OFT septation from its distal to its proximal regions.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the integration of multiple experimental findings.

claim: Fine tuning of BMP signalling levels in cardiac NCC orchestrates OFT septation in time and space.
source: Hence, our findings reveal that fine tuning of BMP signalling levels in cardiac NCC orchestrates OFT septation in time and space.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dullard overexpression in the myogenic cell line C2C12 strongly decreased the levels of phosphorylated Smad1/5/8 induced by BMP2 treatment.
source: As previously shown (Satow et al., 2006), Dullard overexpression in the myogenic cell line C2C12 strongly decreased the levels of phosphorylated Smad1/5/8 induced by BMP2 treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The role of Dullard as negative modulator of BMP signaling relies on its phosphatase activity.
source: In addition, by generating a version of Dullard carrying a phosphatase dead domain, we showed that the role of Dullard as negative modulator of BMP signaling relied on its phosphatase activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data showing that the phosphatase-dead mutant D67E does not inhibit BMP signaling.

claim: Dullard deletion in cardiac NCC was sufficient to double the levels of P-Smad1/5/8 within the NCC whatever their position along the distal-proximal OFT axis of E11.5 hearts.
source: Accordingly, Dullard deletion in cardiac NCC was sufficient to double the levels of P-Smad1/5/8 within the NCC whatever their position along the distal-proximal OFT axis of E11.5 hearts (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of P-Smad1/5/8 immunofluorescence intensity shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The levels of Id1 transcripts were significantly elevated by Dullard loss in cardiac NCC.
source: Quantitative RT-qPCR on isolated E11.5 NCC showed that the levels of Id1 transcripts were significantly elevated by Dullard loss and that Msx1 and Msx2 expression range was shifted towards higher values in mutants compared to control embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Msx1 and Msx2 expression range was shifted towards higher values in Dullard mutant cardiac NCC compared to control embryos.
source: Quantitative RT-qPCR on isolated E11.5 NCC showed that the levels of Id1 transcripts were significantly elevated by Dullard loss and that Msx1 and Msx2 expression range was shifted towards higher values in mutants compared to control embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The amount of Msx2 transcripts detected within the NCC in the vicinity of the aorta was greater in mutants compared to control embryos.
source: In agreement, the amount of Msx2 transcripts detected by in situ hybridisation within the NCC in the vicinity of the aorta was greater in mutants compared to control embryos, so was that of Id2 transcripts present throughout all cardiac NCC (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The amount of Id2 transcripts present throughout all cardiac NCC was greater in mutants compared to control embryos.
source: In agreement, the amount of Msx2 transcripts detected by in situ hybridisation within the NCC in the vicinity of the aorta was greater in mutants compared to control embryos, so was that of Id2 transcripts present throughout all cardiac NCC (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In the cardiac NCC lineage, Dullard acts as a BMP intracellular signalling inhibitor.
source: This further indicates that in the cardiac NCC lineage, Dullard acts as a BMP intracellular signalling inhibitor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing increased BMP signaling in Dullard mutant NCCs.

claim: Dullard was required to dampen the levels of activated Smad1/5/8 in myogenic cells.
source: It is worth mentioning that Dullard was also required to dampen the levels of activated Smad1/5/8 in other cell types, including myogenic cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Dullard has been shown to decrease the levels of phosphorylation of Smads acting downstream of the TGFβ in bone precursors.
source: Furthermore, while Dullard has also been shown to decrease the levels of phosphorylation of Smads acting downstream of the TGF𝞫 in bone precursors (Hayata et al., 2015), the modulation of Dullard activity did not alter the phosphorylation state of one of these Smads, namely Smad2, in cardiac NCC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a statement about Dullard's function in a different cell type, supported by citation.

claim: The modulation of Dullard activity did not alter the phosphorylation state of Smad2 in cardiac NCC.
source: Furthermore, while Dullard has also been shown to decrease the levels of phosphorylation of Smads acting downstream of the TGF𝞫 in bone precursors (Hayata et al., 2015), the modulation of Dullard activity did not alter the phosphorylation state of one of these Smads, namely Smad2, in cardiac NCC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In both control and mutant contexts, P-Smad1/5/8 levels were more elevated distally than proximally along the OFT axis.
source: Remarkably, in both control and mutant contexts, P-Smad1/5/8 levels were more elevated distally than proximally (Figure 1Eiii, Figure 1—figure supplement 1Bii), indicating that BMP signalling elicits a graded response in cardiac NCC, which declines as they colonise more proximal OFT areas.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of P-Smad1/5/8 levels along the OFT axis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: BMP signalling elicits a graded response in cardiac NCC, which declines as they colonise more proximal OFT areas.
source: Remarkably, in both control and mutant contexts, P-Smad1/5/8 levels were more elevated distally than proximally (Figure 1Eiii, Figure 1—figure supplement 1Bii), indicating that BMP signalling elicits a graded response in cardiac NCC, which declines as they colonise more proximal OFT areas.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the P-Smad1/5/8 gradient data.

claim: Dullard is required in cardiac NCC to dampen the magnitude of the BMP signalling gradient along the proximo-distal axis of the OFT.
source: Altogether, our results show that Dullard is required in cardiac NCC to dampen the magnitude of the BMP signalling gradient along the proximo-distal axis of the OFT, but is not required for its establishment, which is still observed in mutant embryos.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that the gradient persists but is amplified in Dullard mutants.

claim: Dullard is not required for the establishment of the BMP signalling gradient along the OFT axis.
source: Altogether, our results show that Dullard is required in cardiac NCC to dampen the magnitude of the BMP signalling gradient along the proximo-distal axis of the OFT, but is not required for its establishment, which is still observed in mutant embryos.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that the gradient persists in Dullard mutants.

claim: No gross morphological defects were detected in E10.5 Dullard mutant OFTs.
source: No gross morphological defects were detected in E10.5 Dullard mutant OFTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The endocardium morphology, the thickness and position of the myocardium, the NCC distribution along the outflow tract, were comparable in control and mutant embryos at E10.5.
source: Notably, the endocardium morphology, the thickness and position of the myocardium, the NCC distribution along the outflow tract, were comparable in control and mutant embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Severe and penetrant morphological OFT defects were observed in Dullard mutant embryos at E11.5.
source: Strikingly, 24 hr later, severe and penetrant morphological OFT defects were observed in Dullard mutant embryos (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by 3D imaging and histological analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: At distal levels, the OFT of control E11.5-12 embryos displayed symmetrical septation with two great arteries of similar size.
source: At distal levels, the OFT of control embryos displayed symmetrical septation with two great arteries of similar size (Figure 2Ai,Bi, Figure 2—figure supplement 1Bi - Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by 3D imaging and histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: Pax3Cre or Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox embryos exhibited an asymmetric breakdown of the endocardium on the pulmonary side with obstruction of the pulmonary artery.
source: In contrast, Pax3Cre or Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox embryos exhibited an asymmetric breakdown of the endocardium on the pulmonary side with obstruction of the pulmonary artery (Pa) (Figure 2Aii,Biv, Figure 2—figure supplement 1Biv - Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by 3D imaging and histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: At medial levels in control E11.5 embryos, the pulmonary pole of the endocardium was still connected to its aortic pole.
source: At more medial levels in control embryos, the pulmonary pole of the endocardium was still connected to its aortic pole (Figure 2Bii, Figure 2—figure supplement 1Bii).
evidence: This is supported by histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: The aortic and pulmonary poles of the endocardium were prematurely septated in the medial portion of the mutant OFT.
source: Conversely, the aortic and pulmonary poles of the endocardium were prematurely septated and the NCC cushions were fused in the medial portion of the mutant OFT (Figure 2Bv, Figure 1—figure supplement 1Bv).
evidence: This is supported by histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: The NCC cushions were fused in the medial portion of the mutant OFT.
source: Conversely, the aortic and pulmonary poles of the endocardium were prematurely septated and the NCC cushions were fused in the medial portion of the mutant OFT (Figure 2Bv, Figure 1—figure supplement 1Bv).
evidence: This is supported by histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: Pulmonary endocardium cells were aggregated together failing to delineate a lumen in Dullard mutants.
source: Similarly to the observations made at distal levels, pulmonary endocardium cells were aggregated together failing to delineate a lumen.
evidence: This is an observation from histological analysis of mutant OFTs.

claim: NCC often intervened between the residual pulmonary endocardium cells and the presumptive pulmonary valve intercalated-cushion (PV-IC) in Dullard mutants.
source: Furthermore, NCC often intervened between the residual pulmonary endocardium cells and the presumptive pulmonary valve intercalated-cushion (PV-IC) (Figure 2Bv).
evidence: This is supported by histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: At proximal regions, the shape of the OFT endocardium and the surrounding NCC cushions were similar in both mutant and control E11.5 embryos.
source: At proximal regions, the shape of the OFT endocardium and the surrounding NCC cushions were similar in both mutant and control embryos (Figure 2A,Biii,vi, Figure 2—figure supplement 1Biii,vi).
evidence: This is supported by histological sections shown in Figure 2.

claim: No significant differences in the peripheral sheet of myocardium could be detected between the control and mutant E11.5 OFTs.
source: We also checked for the state of the peripheral sheet of myocardium composing E11.5 control and Dullard mutant OFTs by immunolabelling the myosin heavy chain or the transcription factor Islet1/2 (Isl1/2) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D). No significant differences could be detected between the control and mutant OFTs.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The premature death of Pax3Cre or Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox embryos occurs after E12.5.
source: In order to evaluate the physiological impact of these OFT defects on cardiac function, we first attempted to harvest older embryos to conduct a histological characterisation of their hearts. The premature death of Pax3Cre or Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox embryos after E12.5 complicated this task (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Dullard mutant embryos collected alive at E14.5 or E18.5 consistently observed hearts with an interventricular septum.

claim: Dullard mutant embryos collected alive at E14.5 or E18.5 showed a hypertrophy of their right ventricle compared to their left one.
source: Nevertheless, in the handful of Dullard mutant embryos collected alive at E14.5 or E18.5, we consistently observed hearts with an interventricular septum (compare Figure 2Dii,iv with 2Di,iii), a hypertrophy of their right ventricle compared to their left one (compare Figure 2Div with 2Diii), a wide aorta connected to both ventricles (Figure 2Dvi, E) and pulmonary stenosis (compare Figure 2Dvi with 2Dv, asterisk in E).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Dullard mutant embryos collected alive at E14.5 or E18.5 showed a wide aorta connected to both ventricles.
source: Nevertheless, in the handful of Dullard mutant embryos collected alive at E14.5 or E18.5, we consistently observed hearts with an interventricular septum (compare Figure 2Dii,iv with 2Di,iii), a hypertrophy of their right ventricle compared to their left one (compare Figure 2Div with 2Diii), a wide aorta connected to both ventricles (Figure 2Dvi, E) and pulmonary stenosis (compare Figure 2Dvi with 2Dv, asterisk in E).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The four major heart morphological traits observed in Dullard mutants define the tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) condition.
source: These are the four major heart morphological traits defining the tetralogy of Fallot (TOF)'s condition (Neeb et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement linking the observed phenotype to a known congenital heart disease, supported by citation.

claim: The systolic velocity peaked at a lower level in E11.75 Dullard mutants compared to controls.
source: Notably, the systolic velocity peaked at a lower level in mutants compared to controls, suggesting a compromised blood ejection from the heart (Figure 2Fi).

claim: The compromised systolic velocity in Dullard mutants suggests a compromised blood ejection from the heart.
source: Notably, the systolic velocity peaked at a lower level in mutants compared to controls, suggesting a compromised blood ejection from the heart (Figure 2Fi).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the hemodynamic data.

claim: No differences in the diastolic velocity were detected between E11.75 Dullard mutants and controls.
source: Conversely, the heart relaxation phase was less affected as no differences in the diastolic velocity were detected (Figure 2Fii).
evidence: This is supported by Doppler ultrasound measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The blood flow was weaker in E11.75 Dullard mutants than in controls, as indicated by a decrease in the mean of the velocity time integral (VTI).
source: Overall, the blood flow was weaker in the mutants than in controls, as indicated by a decrease in the mean of the velocity time integral (VTI) (Figure 2Fiii).
evidence: This is supported by Doppler ultrasound measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: GFP+ cardiac NCC reached similar OFT levels in E11.5 control and Dullard mutants.
source: Whole mount immunostaining and 3D-reconstructions revealed that GFP+ cardiac NCC reached similar OFT levels in E11.5 control and Dullard mutants, showing that Dullard is not required for NCC colonisation of the OFT (Figure 3A, Videos 1–4).
evidence: This is supported by 3D imaging shown in Figure 3A and Videos 1-4.

claim: Dullard is not required for NCC colonisation of the OFT.
source: Whole mount immunostaining and 3D-reconstructions revealed that GFP+ cardiac NCC reached similar OFT levels in E11.5 control and Dullard mutants, showing that Dullard is not required for NCC colonisation of the OFT (Figure 3A, Videos 1–4).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that NCCs reach similar OFT levels in mutants and controls.

claim: Dullard does not control the proliferation of cardiac NCC.
source: Similarly, quantification of cell proliferation and apoptosis on tissue sections, using antibodies raised against the phosphorylated form of histone H3 and the cleaved version of Caspase three respectively, indicated that Dullard does not control the proliferation nor the survival of cardiac NCC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1Ai-iv).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of PH3+ cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Dullard does not control the survival of cardiac NCC.
source: Similarly, quantification of cell proliferation and apoptosis on tissue sections, using antibodies raised against the phosphorylated form of histone H3 and the cleaved version of Caspase three respectively, indicated that Dullard does not control the proliferation nor the survival of cardiac NCC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1Ai-iv).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of cleaved Caspase 3+ cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The total number of GFP+ cells colonising the OFT in mutant embryos was not significantly different from that found in controls.
source: In agreement with these observations, the total number of GFP+ cells colonising the OFT in mutant embryos was not significantly different from that found in controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1Av, vi).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of GFP+ cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The orientation of the cardiac NCC nuclei relative to the endocardium appeared spatially regulated along the proximal-distal axis of the OFT, in both mutant and control hearts.
source: The orientation of the cardiac NCC nuclei relative to the endocardium appeared spatially regulated along the proximal-distal axis of the OFT, in both mutant and control hearts (Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of NCC orientation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In controls, NCC perpendicular to the endocardium could be found at distal levels, while at proximal levels no orientation preference could be assigned.
source: In controls, NCC perpendicular to the endocardium could be found at distal levels, while at proximal levels no orientation preference could be assigned (blue dashes in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of NCC orientation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox OFTs the perpendicular orientation of NCCs was more widely observed at medial levels than in control OFT.
source: Strikingly, in Wnt1Cre; Dullardflox/flox OFTs the perpendicular orientation was more widely observed at medial levels than in control OFT (blue dashes in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of NCC orientation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In E11.5 control hearts, NCC condensation was variable along the distal-proximal axis of the OFT, with cells being closer to each other at distal levels than in proximal regions.
source: Moreover, quantification of the shortest distance between adjacent cardiac NCC nuclei indicated that in E11.5 control hearts NCC condensation was also variable along the distal-proximal axis of the OFT (Figure 3C,Di). Cells were closer to each other at distal levels than in proximal regions.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of inter-NCC distances shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The progression of NCC condensation along the OFT axis was impaired in Dullard mutants, whereby mutant NCC prematurely condensed within the medial region of the OFT.
source: This progression of NCC condensation along the OFT axis was impaired in Dullard mutants, whereby mutant NCC prematurely condensed within the medial region of the OFT (Figure 3C,Di).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of inter-NCC distances shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The position of NCC to the endocardium was variable along the OFT axis of control embryos with NCC being closer to this epithelium at distal levels than at proximal levels.
source: Finally, the position of NCC to the endocardium was variable along the OFT axis of control embryos with NCC being closer to this epithelium at distal levels than at proximal levels (Figure 3C,Dii).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of NCC-endocardium distances shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In Dullard mutants, NCC were in a closer vicinity of the endocardium than control cells.
source: In the mutants, NCC were in a closer vicinity of the endocardium than control cells, so that in medial levels they displayed traits of cells normally found at distal levels in control hearts (Figure 3C,Dii).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of NCC-endocardium distances shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The OFT area was reduced in Dullard mutants and remained more constant along the distal to proximal axis.
source: In agreement with these data, the OFT area was reduced in mutants and remained more constant along the distal to proximal axis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of OFT area shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Dullard precipitates NCC condensation, and thereby leads to the premature breakage of the endocardium and obstruction of the pulmonary artery.
source: Taken together Figures 2 and 3 data demonstrate that Dullard stands as a key modulator of NCC behaviour dynamics in the heart and hence of OFT septation. It precipitates NCC condensation, and thereby leads to the premature breakage of the endocardium and obstruction of the pulmonary artery.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the integration of morphological and cellular data.

claim: The premature breakage of the endocardium and obstruction of the pulmonary artery weakens the embryonic hemodynamics and compromises the living of Dullard mutant embryos.
source: This weakens the embryonic hemodynamics and compromises the living of Dullard mutant embryos (see discussion).
evidence: This is an interpretation linking the morphological defects to the observed lethality.

claim: Morphogenetic defects in the NCC-derived cushions stand as one possible cause of Fallot's tetralogy.
source: Our data also brings further support to the idea that morphogenetic defects in the NCC-derived cushions stand as one possible cause of Fallot's tetralogy (Neeb et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion linking the findings to the etiology of a congenital heart disease, supported by citation.

claim: The 44 chosen genes were sufficient to segregate the three isolated cell subtypes: GFP+ NCC, the RFP+;CD31+ endocardial cells and the other RFP+;CD31- OFT cells.
source: T-statistic Stochastic Neighbour Embedding (t-SNE) was first used to plot the distances existing between the 44 gene-based-transcriptomes of individual cells (Figure 4C). It revealed that the 44 chosen genes were sufficient to segregate the three isolated cell subtypes, GFP+ NCC, the RFP+;CD31+endocardial cells and the other RFP+;CD31- OFT cells, validating our approach.
evidence: This is supported by t-SNE analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis identified six distinct groups of OFT cells.
source: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis of all cells refined this segregation and identified six distinct groups of OFT cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Some groups of OFT cells contained both control and Dullard mutant cells, meaning that their 44 gene-based-transcriptome was not drastically dependent on Dullard.
source: Importantly, some of these groups contained both control and Dullard mutant cells (Groups 1, 3, 5) meaning that their 44 gene-based-transcriptome was not drastically dependent on Dullard.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Three groups of OFT cells were enriched for cells with a given genotype, hence harboured a Dullard dependent transcriptional state.
source: Instead, the three other groups were enriched for cells with a given genotype (Groups 2, 4, 6), hence harboured a Dullard dependent transcriptional state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Most GFP+ NCC were contained in Groups 2, 4, 6, while the other groups were enriched for other cell types.
source: Importantly, most GFP+ NCC were contained in the Groups 2, 4, 6, while the other groups were enriched for other cell types.
evidence: This is an observation from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Dullard deletion in NCC mainly alters the transcriptional states cell-autonomously and modulates to a much lesser extent the surrounding cell types present in the developing E11.5 heart.
source: Overall, it suggests that Dullard deletion in NCC mainly alters the transcriptional states cell-autonomously and modulates to a much lesser extent the surrounding cell types present in the developing E11.5 heart.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that most Dullard-dependent transcriptional changes occur in NCCs.

claim: In both RFP+;CD31+ endocardial cells and RFP+;CD31- OFT cells, some transcriptomic heterogeneity was found and distinct subpopulations could be isolated.
source: Hierarchical clustering and two-dimensional visualisation of cells on diffusion maps indicated that in both cell types, some transcriptomic heterogeneity was found and distinct subpopulations could be isolated (Figure 5Ai–ii', Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by diffusion map analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: All 5 RFP+;CD31- subpopulations identified contained both control and mutant cells.
source: All 5 RFP+;CD31- subpopulations identified contained both control and mutant cells (Figure 5Ai,i'), sustaining the idea that Dullard loss in cardiac NCC does not impair the differentiation of the SHF-derived myocardium and smooth muscle, nor the differentiation of the epicardium (see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by diffusion map analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Dullard loss in cardiac NCC does not impair the differentiation of the SHF-derived myocardium and smooth muscle, nor the differentiation of the epicardium.
source: All 5 RFP+;CD31- subpopulations identified contained both control and mutant cells (Figure 5Ai,i'), sustaining the idea that Dullard loss in cardiac NCC does not impair the differentiation of the SHF-derived myocardium and smooth muscle, nor the differentiation of the epicardium (see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that non-NCC cell types show similar transcriptional profiles in mutants and controls.

claim: The vast majority of RFP+;CD31+ cells (four out of six subpopulations) presented both mutant and control cells.
source: Similarly, the vast majority of RFP+;CD31+ cells (four out of six subpopulations (sub-pops 2 to 5)) presented both mutant and control cells (Figure 5Aii,ii', Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by diffusion map analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The subpopulation 1 of RFP+;CD31+ cells was enriched in control cells while the subpopulation six in mutant cells.
source: However, the subpopulation 1 of RFP+;CD31+ cells was enriched in control cells while the subpopulation six in mutant cells (Figure 5Aii,ii').
evidence: This is supported by diffusion map analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Twist1 and Sox9 were enriched in the subpopulation 1 of RFP+;CD31+ cells.
source: From the genes that drive the segregation of these CD31+ subpopulations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), very few of them were specifically induced or repressed in the subpopulation six or the subpopulation one compared to the others subpopulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C). Out of them stood Twist1 and Sox9, which were enriched in the subpopulation 1.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Few Twist1+ cells could be immunolabelled within the endocardium of control embryos, and these were almost undetectable in mutant embryos.
source: Accordingly, while few Twist1+ cells could be immunolabelled within the endocardium of control embryos, these were almost undetectable in mutant embryos (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Endocardial EMT is affected by the absence of Dullard in the NCC.
source: Twist1 being one of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) drivers, it suggests that endocardial EMT is affected by the absence of Dullard in the NCC (see discussion).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Twist1 expression data in the context of EMT.

claim: Five GFP+ NCC subpopulations were identified based on their gene expression signature.
source: With similar approaches as above we could identify five GFP+ NCC subpopulations based on their gene expression signature (Sub Pops 1 to 5) (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), each of them containing an unbalanced ratio of mutant versus control cells (Figure 5C,D), suggesting that Dullard influences the fate of all NCC subtypes.
evidence: This is supported by diffusion map and clustering analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Each of the five NCC subpopulations contained an unbalanced ratio of mutant versus control cells, suggesting that Dullard influences the fate of all NCC subtypes.
source: With similar approaches as above we could identify five GFP+ NCC subpopulations based on their gene expression signature (Sub Pops 1 to 5) (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), each of them containing an unbalanced ratio of mutant versus control cells (Figure 5C,D), suggesting that Dullard influences the fate of all NCC subtypes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clustering results showing genotype-dependent distribution of cells.

claim: The NCC subpopulation 1 was characterised by the expression of Nfatc1, Tcf21, Postn (Periostin), which are all expressed in the heart valves.
source: The NCC subpopulation 1 was characterised by the expression of Nfatc1, Tcf21, Postn (Periostin) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C), which are all expressed in the heart valves (Acharya et al., 2011; Norris et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2011), a heart structure that is also colonised by NCC (Odelin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis and citations.

claim: The slight enrichment for control cells in NCC subpopulation 1 raised the possibility that Dullard is required to favour the contribution of NCC to the heart valves.
source: The slight enrichment for control cells in this subpopulation raised the possibility that Dullard is required to favour the contribution of NCC to this structure (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cell distribution in subpopulation 1.

claim: The NCC subpopulation 2 was defined by the predominant expression of cardiac progenitor markers Tbx1, Six2, Gja1, Isl1.
source: The second subpopulation was defined by the predominant expression of cardiac progenitor markers Tbx1, Six2, Gja1, Isl1, and contained both control and mutant cardiac NCC (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C), indicating that Dullard is not required for the entry of NCC into the smooth muscle lineage (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: NCC subpopulation 2 contained both control and mutant cardiac NCC, indicating that Dullard is not required for the entry of NCC into the smooth muscle lineage.
source: The second subpopulation was defined by the predominant expression of cardiac progenitor markers Tbx1, Six2, Gja1, Isl1, and contained both control and mutant cardiac NCC (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C), indicating that Dullard is not required for the entry of NCC into the smooth muscle lineage (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that this subpopulation contains both genotypes, supported by citation.

claim: The emergence of the NCC subpopulation 3 was strictly dependent on Dullard, as this subpopulation barely contained mutant cells.
source: Conversely, the emergence of the subpopulation 3 was strictly dependent on Dullard, as this subpopulation barely contained mutant cells (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the cell distribution analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: NCC subpopulation 3 corresponded to NCC further differentiated toward the smooth lineage as defined by expression of Myh11 and Acta2.
source: Subpopulation 3 corresponded to NCC further differentiated toward the smooth lineage as defined by expression of Myh11 and Acta2 (Huang et al., 2008; Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis and citation.

claim: The NCC subpopulations 4 and 5 were enriched for mutant cardiac NCC.
source: The subpopulations 4 and 5 were enriched for mutant cardiac NCC (Figure 5C–E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the cell distribution analysis shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: The transcriptomic state of the cells in NCC subpopulations 4 and 5 diverged from that of the subpopulation 3 cells.
source: The transcriptomic state of the cells in these two subpopulations diverged from that of the subpopulation 3 cells (Figure 5C,E,D).
evidence: This is an observation from the gene expression analysis.

claim: The position of cells within the diffusion maps suggests a close relationship between NCC subpopulations 4 and 5 which might represent two states of the differentiation path of Dullard deleted cardiac NCC.
source: Yet, the position of cells within the diffusion maps suggests a close relationship between these two subsets of cells which might represent two states of the differentiation path of Dullard deleted cardiac NCC (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the diffusion map topology.

claim: The levels of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Cdh2, Mmp14, Rac1) in NCC subpopulations 4 and 5 were lower than in the subpopulation 3.
source: Strikingly, genes that were differentially expressed between subpopulation 3 and the subpopulation 4/5 encode for known regulators of cell adhesion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. On the one hand, the levels of mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1, Cdh2, Mmp14, Rac1) in both subpopulations 4 and 5 were lower than in the subpopulation 3.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: In control embryos, NCC expressing mesenchymal markers (Snai2, Twist1) were found near the endocardium.
source: In control embryos, NCC expressing these markers were found near the endocardium, as demonstrated by an ISH for Snai2 or immunolabelling for Twist1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In Dullard mutants, pro-epithelial-mesenchymal transition factors (Snai2, Twist1) were barely detected in NCC.
source: In mutants, these pro-epithelial-mesenchymal transition factors were barely detected in NCC.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The downregulation of mesenchymal markers in Dullard mutants is in agreement with the NCC over-condensation phenotype observed nearby the endocardium.
source: These data are in agreement with the NCC over-condensation phenotype observed in Dullard mutants nearby the endocardium.
evidence: This is an interpretation linking the gene expression changes to the cellular phenotype.

claim: Cells in NCC subpopulations 4 and 5 displayed higher levels of the epithelial markers Cdh5 and Sema3c compared to subpopulation 3 cells.
source: On the other hand, cells in subpopulations 4 and 5 displayed higher levels of the epithelial markers Cdh5 and of Sema3c compared to subpopulation 3 cells.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: In situ hybridization of Sema3c confirmed the elevated expression in Dullard mutant NCCs.
source: In situ hybridization of Sema3c further confirmed these results with cellular resolution (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B), showing that at distal OFT levels, Sema3C was expressed in a scattered fashion in NCC in cushions of control embryos, while it was found in almost all NCC in mutants.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At distal OFT levels, Sema3C was expressed in a scattered fashion in NCC in cushions of control embryos, while it was found in almost all NCC in mutants.
source: In situ hybridization of Sema3c further confirmed these results with cellular resolution (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B), showing that at distal OFT levels, Sema3C was expressed in a scattered fashion in NCC in cushions of control embryos, while it was found in almost all NCC in mutants.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A graded decrease of Sema3c expression along the OFT axis was observed in both control and mutant embryos.
source: Importantly, we observed a graded decrease of Sema3c expression along the OFT axis in both control and mutant embryos.
evidence: This is an observation from in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The graded decrease of Sema3c expression along the OFT axis was reminiscent of the BMP response and condensation gradients.
source: This was reminiscent of the BMP response and condensation gradients described previously (Figures 1E and 3D) and in agreement with the established role of Sema3c in the regulation of cohesive/metastatic balance in several cancers (Tamagnone, 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation linking the Sema3c gradient to the BMP and condensation gradients, supported by citation.

claim: Dullard prevents the establishment of an epithelial-like state in NCC.
source: Altogether, our results show that Dullard prevents the establishment of an epithelial-like state and promotes the expression of pro-mesenchymal genes in NCC.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the gene expression data.

claim: Dullard promotes the expression of pro-mesenchymal genes in NCC.
source: Altogether, our results show that Dullard prevents the establishment of an epithelial-like state and promotes the expression of pro-mesenchymal genes in NCC.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the gene expression data.

claim: Dullard may impair the epithelial mesenchymal transition of the endothelial cells.
source: In addition, it may also impair the epithelial mesenchymal transition of the endothelial cells (see discussion).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observation of altered Twist1 expression in the endocardium.

claim: A BMP-dependent gradient of cardiac NCC condensation sets the timing of cardiac cushions fusion and thereby the septation of the OFT into the aorta and pulmonary artery.
source: Our analysis of the functions of the Dullard phosphatase in cardiac NCC brings us to propose a model whereby a BMP-dependent gradient of cardiac NCC condensation would set the timing of cardiac cushions fusion and thereby the septation of the OFT into the aorta and pulmonary artery.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the integration of all experimental findings.

claim: The phenotype of Dullard mutant mice is analogous to patients suffering from Fallot's tetralogy condition.
source: In addition, the analogy between the phenotype of Dullard mutant mice and patients suffering from Fallot's tetralogy condition calls for a discussion on the cellular and molecular aetiology of this complex congenital heart disease.
evidence: This is a statement linking the mouse model to human disease.

claim: A gradient of BMP activation exists in the cardiac NCC along the OFT axis and matches with a gradient of NCC condensation.
source: First, we showed that a gradient of BMP activation exists in the cardiac NCC along the OFT axis and matches with a gradient of NCC condensation.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing correlated gradients.

claim: The magnitude of the BMP gradient in cardiac NCC is under the control of the phosphatase Dullard.
source: The magnitude of this BMP gradient is under the control of the phosphatase Dullard.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that the gradient is amplified in Dullard mutants.

claim: The establishment of the BMP gradient in cardiac NCC is dependent on mechanisms other than Dullard, as the gradient is still observed in absence of Dullard.
source: Yet, the establishment of this gradient is dependent on other mechanisms, as the gradient is still observed in absence of Dullard in the cardiac NCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the persistence of the gradient in Dullard mutants.

claim: The establishment of the BMP gradient is unlikely to result from a corresponding gradient of ligand that would diffuse from a localized distal source.
source: The establishment of this gradient is unlikely to result from a corresponding gradient of ligand that would diffuse from a localized distal source, as described in other contexts (Bier and De Robertis, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of gradient formation, supported by citation.

claim: BMP4 is homogeneously expressed in the myocardium throughout the entire length of the OFT and not solely at the distal level.
source: In fact, BMP4 is homogeneously expressed in the myocardium throughout the entire length of the OFT and not solely at the distal level (Jia et al., 2007; Jiao et al., 2003; Jones et al., 1991; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about BMP4 expression pattern, supported by citations.

claim: Intracellular signalling inhibitors could allow a temporal adaptation of cardiac NCC to BMP signals along with their migration towards proximal levels of the OFT.
source: Rather, intracellular signalling inhibitors could allow a temporal adaptation of cardiac NCC to BMP signals along with their migration towards proximal levels of the OFT.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of gradient formation.

claim: Prominent expression of Smad6, a BMP negative feedback effector, is observed in the OFT from E10.5 throughout the great arteries formation.
source: Prominent expression of Smad6, a BMP negative feedback effector, and of the diffusible inhibitor Noggin, are indeed observed in the OFT from E10.5 throughout the great arteries formation and thus represent promising candidates (Choi et al., 2007; Galvin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement about the expression of BMP inhibitors, supported by citations.

claim: Prominent expression of the diffusible inhibitor Noggin is observed in the OFT from E10.5 throughout the great arteries formation.
source: Prominent expression of Smad6, a BMP negative feedback effector, and of the diffusible inhibitor Noggin, are indeed observed in the OFT from E10.5 throughout the great arteries formation and thus represent promising candidates (Choi et al., 2007; Galvin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement about the expression of BMP inhibitors, supported by citations.

claim: Several lines of evidence support the idea that the elevation of BMP signalling in Dullard mutants underpins the premature condensation of cardiac NCC and the strong pulmonary artery atrophy.
source: Secondly, several lines of evidence support the idea that the elevation of BMP signalling in Dullard mutants underpins the premature condensation of cardiac NCC and the strong pulmonary artery atrophy.
evidence: This is a summary statement integrating multiple pieces of evidence.

claim: In other biological systems, Dullard loss has been associated with decreased Wnt-β-Catenin signalling.
source: While in other biological systems, Dullard loss has been associated with decreased Wnt-𝞫-Catenin signalling (Tanaka et al., 2013) or enhanced TGF𝞫-Smads2/3 signalling (Hayata et al., 2015), these signalling pathways are probably not affected upon Dullard deletion in the cardiac NCC.
evidence: This is a statement about Dullard's function in other contexts, supported by citation.

claim: In other biological systems, Dullard loss has been associated with enhanced TGFβ-Smads2/3 signalling.
source: While in other biological systems, Dullard loss has been associated with decreased Wnt-𝞫-Catenin signalling (Tanaka et al., 2013) or enhanced TGF𝞫-Smads2/3 signalling (Hayata et al., 2015), these signalling pathways are probably not affected upon Dullard deletion in the cardiac NCC.
evidence: This is a statement about Dullard's function in other contexts, supported by citation.

claim: Wnt and TGFβ signalling pathways are probably not affected upon Dullard deletion in the cardiac NCC.
source: While in other biological systems, Dullard loss has been associated with decreased Wnt-𝞫-Catenin signalling (Tanaka et al., 2013) or enhanced TGF𝞫-Smads2/3 signalling (Hayata et al., 2015), these signalling pathways are probably not affected upon Dullard deletion in the cardiac NCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lack of changes in Smad2 phosphorylation and the phenotypic differences from Wnt loss-of-function.

claim: Loss of Wnt signalling in cardiac NCC leads to persistent truncus arteriosus, which is associated with reduced NCC-mediated cushion fusion.
source: On the one hand, we showed that the phosphorylation state of Smad2 in Dullard mutant and control cardiac NCC was comparable (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
